fields.title: Retention strategy: processes, not mechanics
fields.keyTakeaway: The plan for active clients relies not on notifications, but on several processes: guiding to first value, addressing churn signals, and win-back of lost customers. Each of them has an owner and a metric.
fields.checkQuestion: Churn grew by 2 percentage points. Which three processes will you check first?
fields.blocks/0/text: The key question of this node: **which processes will deliver the active user targets?**
fields.blocks/1/text: **What happens if you don't answer this question.** Nobody owns retention: marketing acquires, product builds features, support responds. Churn grows slowly and is only discovered after plans have already been made.
fields.blocks/2/subtitle: Each has an owner, a metric, and a response timeframe
fields.blocks/2/items/0: **Guiding to first value**—from payment to the moment after which churn stops. Metric: share of users reaching it in N days.
fields.blocks/2/items/1: **Early warning**—signs of imminent churn: stopped logging in, transaction volume dropped, key person on the customer side left. Metric: share of at-risk customers and share of retained ones.
fields.blocks/2/items/2: **Win-back of churned users**—a separate process with its own offer; some churned customers return if the issue was fixed and communicated.
fields.blocks/2/items/3: **Essential addition:** the reason for churn is recorded based on real facts, not a checkbox in a cancellation form.
fields.blocks/3/text:
First value: create and sign a document. Owner—product team, metric—share of users reaching it within 7 days (currently 52%).

Early warning: client hasn't created a single document in 14 days. The list goes to support once a week: they reach out to the person and ask what is blocking them. Of those contacted, 44% stay versus 21% among similar clients who were not contacted.

Win-back: once a quarter, clients who churned in the past six months get an email about what has changed. 6% return—cheap and predictable.

Support collects churn reasons in conversation, not via a form: the vague "don't use it" turns into specific feedback in about half the cases.
fields.blocks/3/title: Reestr, how it is set up
fields.blocks/4/text: A discount postpones churn and ruins unit economics: a customer retained with price usually leaves at the next renewal. Fixing the cause works, while money serves only as a gesture in case of a clear mistake on your part.
fields.blocks/4/title: Retention cannot be bought with a renewal discount
fields.blocks/5/text: Some churn is healthy: the customer grew out of it, closed down, or the task disappeared. The goal is not zero churn, but zero churn caused by preventable issues; telling them apart has to be done manually.
